summary:
InSAR.Almaty is an automated operational seismic risk monitoring and early-warning control center built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge to protect the megacity of Almaty and the Northern Tien Shan zone.We developed an interactive MVP dashboard using Python, Streamlit, and Folium that integrates NASA Earthdata (NISAR L+S Band GUNW interferograms via asf-search) and real-time USGS seismic feeds to monitor crustal deformation and tectonic stress 24/7.
The platform addresses the challenge through a rigorous Dual Verification Gate that combines magnitude cutoffs (M >= 4.5) with critical InSAR surface displacement thresholds and atmospheric noise filtering, effectively eliminating false alarms. Upon detecting a validated threat within 100 km, the system automatically computes the nearest safe assembly point and dispatches instant Telegram alerts containing Google Maps navigation routes.
This project is vital because it safeguards over 2 million residents in a high-risk seismic zone, minimizing public panic through multi-factor validation and providing actionable evacuation paths. Furthermore, its architecture is fully scalable and ready for deployment in any seismically active region worldwide.
details:
Project Overview & Architecture

InSAR.Almaty is an automated operational seismic risk monitoring and early-warning control center designed specifically for the megacity of Almaty and the Northern Tien Shan seismogenic zone. Developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge, it provides a robust solution for real-time tectonic stress monitoring and emergency evacuation management.

How It Works & Core Innovation

The platform solves the critical issue of false alarms in earthquake early warning by introducing a rigorous Dual Verification Gate. It combines real-time seismic data feeds (USGS API for earthquakes with M >= 4.5) with high-resolution NASA radar spectra (NISAR L+S Band GUNW interferograms retrieved via asf-search).

  • Atmospheric & Noise Filtering: Raw radar data undergoes advanced noise removal, Gaussian de-trending, and median filtering to extract genuine crustal deformation while filtering out atmospheric interference.
  • Automated Alerts & Evacuation: When a validated seismic event (M >= 4.5 within 100 km) occurs, the system automatically computes the nearest safe assembly point and dispatches instant push notifications via Telegram, complete with direct Google Maps navigation links.

Tech Stack & Tools

  • Programming Language & Core Logic: Python.
  • Web Dashboard & UI: Streamlit for interactive control, custom CSS for styling and metric cards.
  • GIS & Spatial Analysis: Folium, streamlit-folium, and rasterio for processing GeoTIFF NISAR interferograms and rendering interactive maps with active tectonic faults (Almaty, Zailiyskiy, Kemin-Chilik zones).
  • Data APIs: NASA Earthdata (asf-search) and USGS Earthquake API (24/7 automated synchronization).

Impact & Scalability

The project safeguards over 2 million residents of Almaty by minimizing public panic through multi-factor validation and providing immediate, actionable evacuation paths. Furthermore, the architecture is fully modular and scalable, allowing instant deployment for any seismically active megacity worldwide.
